questions.q: Which trigger turns a flow into a scheduled cloud flow instead of one that reacts to an event?
options: When an item is created
Recurrence
Manually trigger a flow
When a data driven alert is triggered
questions.explain: The Recurrence trigger is what makes a flow run on a schedule — minute, hour, day, week, or month — rather than in response to a connector event.

questions.q: Castlebridge Logistics wants its flow to run every two weeks. How should Interval and Frequency be set?
options: Interval 2, Frequency Week
Interval 1, Frequency Week
Interval 14, Frequency Day
Interval 2, Frequency Month
questions.explain: Interval is the number of units between runs, and Frequency is the unit. Interval 2 with Frequency Week means the flow runs every two weeks.

questions.q: In what time standard must a Recurrence trigger's Start time always be entered?
options: Whatever local time zone the flow's owner is in
Coordinated Universal Time (UTC)
The time zone of the SharePoint site being used
Start time has no time component, only a date
questions.explain: Start time is always entered in UTC, in the format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ, regardless of where the person configuring the flow is physically located.

questions.q: What is the practical difference between configuring Recurrence in the new designer versus the classic designer?
options: The classic designer cannot configure Recurrence at all
The fields are different between the two designers
Both designers expose the same settings, but the classic designer requires expanding "Show advanced options" first
The new designer only works for flows created after 2026
questions.explain: Both designers configure the same Interval, Frequency, and time-zone fields — the new designer opens a configuration pane directly, while the classic designer needs "Show advanced options" expanded first.

questions.q: Why does Castlebridge Logistics's flow call convertFromUtc() on the Recurrence trigger's timestamp?
options: Because the flow would not run at all without it
To convert the UTC-based trigger time into Eastern time for a human-readable run log
Because Recurrence triggers cannot store a timestamp otherwise
To change the flow's actual schedule to Eastern time
questions.explain: The Recurrence trigger always operates in UTC. convertFromUtc() translates that timestamp into a named local time zone purely for display, such as logging when a scheduled run actually happened in Eastern time.
